stories.title: Universal Studios Japan to spend up to $2.4 billion on expansion: Nikkei
stories.summary: Universal Studios Japan plans a major expansion costing up to $2.4 billion, using a 60,000 sq m site next to the park for new attractions. The expansion aims to increase annual visitors beyond 16 million, the highest attendance among Japanese theme parks. The park will extend onto a former Nippon Steel factory site, with a lease expected by 2028 from Osaka city, but the company has not officially confirmed plans. Universal Studios Japan is preparing to undertake a major expansion, with investment expected to total between 200 billion yen and 300 billion yen (S$1.59 billion-$2.39 billion), the Nikkei newspaper reported on Aug 28. Universal Japan plans to use a 60,000 sq m site adjacent to the theme park to build new attractions, marking the first time the venue has grown its footprint since it opened in 2001, the report said. The company aims to boost its annual attendance above the current 16 million visitors, already the highest among the country’s theme parks, as more overseas tourists visit Japan, Nikkei said. Nikkei added that Universal Japan will extend its grounds on to a former Nippon Steel factory site north of its current property, with the park’s operator expected to sign a lease agreement with the Osaka municipal government around 2028 for the portion of the site owned by the city.

stories.title: Tiger, Futu post strong overseas gains after Beijing clampdown stalls mainland growth
stories.summary: Tiger Brokers and Futu Holdings, two of the region’s largest online brokerages, posted robust second-quarter growth as they expanded overseas to absorb Beijing’s toughest crackdown yet on illegal cross-border stock trading. UP Fintech Holding, parent of Tiger Brokers, reported on Wednesday that revenue rose 31.4 per cent year on year to a record US$182.3 million.
